body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
solution: ① 배고픔이 불편함과 부정적인 감정을 유발한다고 명시되어 있으므로 지문의 내용과 일치한다. ② 해당 슬로건은 패스트푸드 회사가 아니라 캔디바(candy bar) 광고 슬로건이라고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ 'hangry'는 여러 국제 사전에 공식 영어 단어로 등재되었다고 했으므로, 삭제되었다는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ④ 'hangry'는 'happy'와 'angry'의 합성어가 아니라 'hungry'와 'angry'의 합성어라고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 식사 후 배부름이 업무 성과를 향상시킨다는 직접적인 진술은 지문에 없으므로 일치하지 않는다.
choices: Hunger causes discomfort and often leads to negative emotions.
"You're not you when you're hungry" is a slogan from a fast food company.
The word "hangry" was recently removed from international dictionaries.
"Hangry" is a combination of the words "happy" and "angry."
Feeling full after a meal always improves a person's work performance.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절 한 곳을 고르시오.
Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. ( ⓐ ) When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. ( ⓑ ) It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. ( ⓒ ) But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. ( ⓓ ) The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. ( ⓔ ) These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.
solution: 주어진 문장은 코르티솔 수치 상승이 심박수·혈압 증가 및 불안, 짜증, 우울 등의 심리적 효과로 이어진다는 내용으로, 'Elevated cortisol levels'라는 표현이 앞 문장에서 코르티솔이 언급된 이후에 등장해야 자연스럽다. ⑤ 앞 문장에서는 인체가 코르티솔을 분비함으로써 위협에 반응한다고 설명하고 있으며, ⑤ 뒤 문장에서는 이러한 생리적 반응들이 심리학 연구와 일치하는 것으로 보인다고 마무리하고 있다. 주어진 문장이 코르티솔의 구체적인 생리· 심리적 효과를 제시하고, 뒤 문장이 그 반응들을 'These physiological reactions'로 지칭하며 종합하는 구조이므로, 따라서 코르티솔 분비가 언급된 직후이자 생리적 반응 전체를 요약하는 마지막 문장 직전인 ⑤ 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.
choices: ⓔ 1회차 실전 모의고사

다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A),
(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? Skipping breakfast due to a(n) (A) morning routine can negatively affect a student's ability to (B) _____ in class.
solution: (A) Jenny는 아르바이트 후 늦게 잠들고 버스를 타기 위해 서두르다 아침을 거른 상황이므로, 바쁘게 서두르는 아침 일과를 나타내는 'rushed(서두르는)'가 가장 적절하다. (B) 수업 시간에 집중하지 못하고 연필을 두드리거나 시계를 째려보는 등 학업에 어려움을 겪는 내용이 이어지므로, 'concentrate(집중하다)'가 가장 적절하다. 비상(홍) 3과
choices: rushed ― concentrate
rushed ― perform
ordinary ― concentrate
busy ― participate

After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. 이 슬로건 이 의미하는 것은 배고픔이 당신의 기분과 수행 능력을 심 각하게 바꿀 수 있다는 것이다. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
조건 1. 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
2. (means, hunger, seriously, your mood, change, can) 단어를 모두 포함할 것
3. 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것
→
answer: What this slogan means is that hunger can seriously change your mood and performance.
solution: 정답 문장은 'What this slogan means is that hunger can seriously change your mood and performance.'이다. 관계대명사 'what'으로 시작하는 명사절 'What this slogan means'가 주어 역할을 하며, 보어 자리에 명사절 접속사 'that'을 사용하여 'that hunger can seriously change your mood and performance'를 연결한다. 박스에서 제공된 'means', 'hunger', 'seriously', 'your mood', 'change', 'can'을 모두 활용하고, 명사절 접속사 'that'은 학생이 스스로 추가해야 한다. 'change'는 조동사 'can' 뒤에 오므로 원형 그대로 사용하며, 목적어로 'your mood and performance'를 써야 완전한 문장이 된다.

body:
다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 없는 것은?
Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? 1회차 실전 모의고사
solution: ③ 지문에서 Jenny의 반 친구들은 그녀의 기분을 알아채기 시작했고(start noticing her mood), 심지어 배에서 나는 소리를 비웃기까지 했다고 나와 있으므로, 친구들이 Jenny의 불편한 상태를 몰랐다고 추론할 수 없다. ① Jenny가 아르바이트를 마친 후 과제를 하느라 늦게 잠들었다는 내용을 통해 학업과 아르바이트 두 가지가 모두 원인임을 추론할 수 있다. ② 아침을 거른 것이 상황을 더 악화시켰다(made matters worse)고 했으므로, 아침을 먹었다면 더 잘 준비할 수 있었을 것이라 추론할 수 있다. ④ 배가 고파질수록 Jenny가 연필을 두드리고 시계를 째려보다가 결국 친구들에게 화를 냈다는 내용을 통해 배고픔이 감정 조절을 어렵게 했음을 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 마지막 문장에서 독자에게 "Have you ever felt like Jenny?"라고 질문하는 것은 이 경험이 많은 학생들에게 공감될 수 있음을 암시한다.
choices: Jenny's late night was caused by both schoolwork and a part-time job.
Jenny would have been better prepared for class if she had eaten breakfast.
Jenny's classmates were unaware of her uncomfortable physical condition.
Jenny's hunger made it harder for her to control her emotions.
The experience described in the passage is likely relatable to many students.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
Jenny was up late last night ⓐfinishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters
ⓑmore badly because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class
ⓒdragging on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start
ⓓnoticed her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever ⓔfeeling like Jenny?
solution: ① 'finishing'은 'was up late last night finishing'에서 분사구문으로 쓰였으며, Jenny가 과제를 마무리하는 능동적 행위를 나타내므로 현재분사 finishing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ② more badly → worse 'made matters worse'는 관용적 비교 표현으로, worse가 올바른 형태이다. badly의 비교급은 worse이며, more badly는 비문법적이다. ③ dragging → drags 'As the class drags on'에서 As절의 주어 the class에 대한 동사가 필요하다. 현재분사 dragging은 단독으로 절의 서술어가 될 수 없으므로, 단순현재 동사 drags로 고쳐야 한다. ④ noticed → noticing 'start'는 to부정사 또는 동명사를 목적어로 취하며, 'start noticing'처럼 능동의 동명사가 와야 한다. noticed는 과거분사로 이 자리에 올 수 없다. ⑤ feeling → felt 현재완료 구조(have p.p.)를 취하기 위해 'Have you ever feeling like Jenny?'에서 feeling을 felt로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 없는 것은?
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
solution: ④ 'hangry' 현상은 매우 흔하다고 했으며, 이 단어가 여러 국제 사전에 공식 영어 단어로 등재되었다고 하였다. 이는 특정 문화권에 한정된 현상이 아니라 보편적인 현상임을 암시하므로, 특정 문화권에서만 나타난다는 진술은 추론할 수 없다. ① 배고픔이 불쾌감, 무기력함, 부정적 감정을 유발한다고 했으므로, 배고픔이 부정적 감정을 더 유발한다는 것을 추론할 수 있다. ② 식사 후에는 배부르고 행복하며 편안한 반면, 배고플 때는 불쾌감과 부정적 감정이 생긴다고 했으므로 두 상태가 대조된다고 추론할 수 있다. ③ 'hangry'는 hungry와 angry의 조합이라고 본문에 명시되어 있으므로 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ "배고플 때는 당신이 아니다"라는 광고 슬로건이 배고픔이 기분과 수행 능력을 바꾼다는 의미라고 했으므로, 슬로건이 배고픔과 기분 변화의 관계를 반영한다고 추론할 수 있다.
choices: 배고픔은 긍정적인 감정보다 부정적인 감정을 더 유발하기 쉽다.
식사 후의 심리적 상태는 배고픔 상태와 대조된다.
'hangry'라는 단어는 배고픔과 분노의 합성어로 만들어졌 다.
'hangry' 현상은 특정 문화권에서만 나타나는 독특한 감정 이다.
광고 슬로건이 배고픔과 기분 변화의 관계를 반영하기도 한 다.

For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. solution: 먼저 'result'를 정답 문장의 주어로 사용하되 복수형 'results'로 변형한다. 동사 'show'는 과거 시제 'showed'로 변형하며, 명사절 접속사 조건에 따라 'showed' 뒤에 'that'을 스스로 추가하여 명사절을 이끈다. 명사절 안에서는 'participant'를 복수형 'participants'로 변형하고, 관계대명사 조건에 따라 'participants' 뒤에 관계대명사 'who'를 스스로 추가하여 관계절 'who skipped eating'을 구성한다. 이때 동사 'skip'은 과거형 'skipped'로, 'eat'은 'eating'으로 변형한다. 주절의 동사는 'had'이며, 형용사 'poor'는 비교급 'poorer'로 변형하여 'poorer performance'를 만든다. 비교 대상은 'than those who ate beforehand'로 구성하며, 'eat'은 과거형 'ate'로 변형한다. 최종 정답: The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.
solution: ① 배고프다고 해서 모든 사람이 짜증을 내는 것은 아니며, 개인마다 유전자·성격·생활방식·경험에 따라 반응이 다르다고 명시되어 있으므로 일치한다. ② 과일파리는 음식이 부족할 때 덜 활동적이 되는 것이 아니라 더 공격적이 된다고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ 물고기는 배고플 때 집단 결속력이 강해지는 것이 아니라 줄어든다고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ④ 글에서 사람들은 부정적 감정을 인식하면 조절할 수 있다고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 글에서는 점심을 거른 것을 예로 들었을 뿐, 저녁 식사를 거르는 것을 주된 원인으로 제시하지 않았으므로 일치하지 않는다.

Psychology is not the only field of science
ⓐconcerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets ⓑabsorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from ⓒperforming what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone ⓓwhich helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and
ⓔdepressed.
solution: ⑤가 정답이다. ⑤ depressed → depression 'along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and ~'에서 밑줄 친 부분은 앞의 명사 anxiety, irritation과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 한다. 따라서 형용사 depressed가 아니라 명사 depression을 써야 한다. ① concern은 '~에 관한'의 의미로 앞의 명사 field of science를 수식하는 과거분사로 쓰였다. field가 '관련된' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 concerned가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 주어 It(glucose)이 세포에 의해 '흡수되는' 수동의 의미이므로, 'get+과거분사' 형태의 수동태 absorbed가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 전치사 from의 목적어로 동명사가 와야 하므로 performing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 선행사 a hormone을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로, 선행사가 사물이므로 which가 올바르게 쓰였다.

For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.
solution: ① 배고픔에 대한 개인차를 설명하면서 배고픔이 부정적 감정 (anger)을 유발할 수 있으며, 이를 인식하면 조절할 수 있다고 조언하는 글이므로, 글의 목적으로 가장 적절하다. ② 글의 첫 문장에서 배고프다고 해서 모두가 짜증을 내는 것은 아니라고 명시하고 있으므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ 과일파리와 물고기의 반응은 배고픔과 행동의 연관성을 뒷받침하는 사례로 언급된 것일 뿐, 글의 목적은 아니다. ④ 식사를 거르는 것의 위험성 경고는 글에서 직접 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 유전자가 배고픔 반응을 결정한다는 주장은 개인차의 한 요인으로 언급된 것일 뿐, 글 전체의 목적이 아니다. 비상(홍) 3과

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long- term solution due to health risks. Interestingly, the human brain's response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
solution: ③ 고독감이 신체적 허기를 유발하는 '외로운 허기' 현상과, 외로움이 허기와 동일한 뇌 반응을 일으키는 사회적 결핍 신호라는 내용이 지문 전체를 관통하므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ① 정서적 식사는 외로움을 단기적으로 해소하는 한 가지 사례로만 언급되었을 뿐, 글 전체의 핵심인 고독감과 허기의 연결 메커니즘을 포괄하지 못한다. ② 뇌 영상 연구는 외로움과 허기의 뇌 반응이 유사함을 뒷받침하는 근거로 제시된 것이지, 사회적 행동을 밝히는 것이 글의 요지는 아니다. ④ 정서적 식사의 장기적 건강 위험은 도입부에서 잠깐 언급된 부분적 내용일 뿐, 글 전체가 전달하고자 하는 고독감과 허기의 연결 관계를 담지 못한다. ⑤ 사회적 영양이 신체적 음식을 대체한다는 내용은 지문에 언급되지 않았다.
choices: Emotional Eating: A Short-Term Fix for Loneliness
How Brain Imaging Studies Reveal Social Behavior
Lonely Hunger: When Isolation Triggers Physical Craving

Social Nourishment as a Substitute for Physical Food

3. 필요 시 어형을 변형할 것

answer: a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
solution: 정답 문장은 'a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.'이다. 먼저 박스에 제공된 'result'는 주어 'a lack of social nourishment'에 수를 일치시켜 3인칭 단수 현재형 'results'로 변형한다. 'feeling'은 'feelings of social hunger'처럼 복수형 'feelings'로 변형하며, 전치사 'of'를 활용해 'feelings of social hunger'를 구성한다. 'deficit'은 동격 표현으로 'social hunger' 뒤에 이어지며, 문법 조건인 관계대명사 'that'을 학생이 직접 추가하여 'a deficit that needs to be addressed' 구조를 완성한다. 이때 'need'는 'needs'로 어형을 변형하고, 수동태 조건에 따라 학생이 'be addressed'를 스스로 추가하여 'needs to be addressed'의 수동태 구조를 완성해야 한다. 박스에서 제공된 'to'는 'needs to be addressed'의 'to'로 활용된다. 결과적으로 관계대명사 'that'과 수동태 'be addressed'가 결합된 복합 구문이 완성된다.

body:

Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? ⓐ Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. ⓑ Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! ⓒ So you can blame your genes if you don't like those foods. But wait, there's more! ⓓ Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. ⓔ While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work? The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to support that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control. A psychological experiment found that hunger can (A) _____ cognitive and behavioral performance, which supports the popular belief that being hungry can make people more (B) .
solution: (A) 지문에서 실험 결과 식사를 거른 참가자들이 식사를 한 참가자들보다 더 낮은 수행을 보였고, Stroop 과제에서도 더 많은 오류를 범했다고 했으며, 결론적으로 빈속이 주의력과 자제력을 '낮춘다'고 했으므로, 배고픔이 인지 행동적 수행을 '저하시킨다'는 의미의 'undermine'이 적절하다. 다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 없는 것은?
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.

While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger ⓐcausing by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel ⓑlonelily and isolated from others, often ⓒlooked for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way ⓓto relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long- term solution ⓔdue that health risks.
solution: ④ 'Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions'에서 'way'를 수식하는 to부정사 to relieve가 올바르게 쓰였다. 'a way to do'는 '~하는 방법'이라는 뜻의 정형화된 표현으로, to부정사가 명사 way를 수식하는 형용사적 용법으로 쓰인 것이다. 따라서 ④가 정답이다. ① causing by → caused by 분사 causing은 능동의 의미를 나타내므로 'causing by'는 어법상 불가하다. '신체적 필요에 의해 야기된'이라는 수동의 의미이므로, 과거분사 caused를 써서 caused by로 고쳐야 한다. ② lonelily → lonely 동사 feel은 '~한 상태이다'를 뜻하는 연결동사(linking verb)이므로, 뒤에 부사가 아니라 형용사 보어가 와야 한다. 따라서 부사 lonelily는 형용사 lonely로 고쳐야 한다. ③ looked for → looking for 'often looked for a comfort'는 앞 절의 주어 some people을 의미상 주어로 하는 분사구문이다. some people이 능동적으로 위안을 찾는 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 looked for가 아니라 능동의 현재분사 looking for로 고쳐야 한다. ⑤ due that → due to due to는 '~ 때문에'라는 뜻의 전치사구로, 뒤에 명사(구)가 온다. that은 접속사로 명사절을 이끌 수 있으나, due는 접속사와 결합하는 구조가 아니다. 따라서 due that을 due to로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Psychology is not the only field of science (A)[concerned / concerning] with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing (B)[that / what] they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels (C)[lead / leading] to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

(C) 문장의 주어는 'Elevated cortisol levels'로 복수명사이며, 이 문장은 별도의 본동사가 필요한 완전한 절이므로 동사 lead가 적절하다. leading을 쓰면 문장에 본동사가 없어져 불완전한 문장이 된다.

ⓑcause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. ⓒwhich can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, ⓓwhile the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making ⓔare greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry."

Does this mean that everyone ⓐwho is hungry gets irritated about something? ⓒlinking to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able ⓓto recognize them. solution: ⓒ linking → linked 수동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 현재분사가 아닌 과거분사가 필요하다. 'the behavior of many animals'는 nourishment의 가용성에 '연결되는' 것이 아니라 '연결되어 있는' 대상이므로, be동사 뒤에서 수동태를 이루는 과거분사 linked가 와야 한다. is closely linking은 능동의 현재분사 형태로 수동의 의미를 나타낼 수 없으므로 어법상 틀렸다. ⓔ That → What 이 문장에서 밑줄 친 부분은 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 한다. 다음 중 영영풀이와 단어가 잘못 연결된 것은?
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.
ⓐvary: to always stay the same without any change
ⓑaggressive: acting in an angry or violent way toward others
ⓒhungry: wanting or needing food
ⓓcontrol: to have power over something and decide what happens
ⓔrecognize: to know and remember someone or something you have seen before
solution: ① 제시된 풀이 '변화 없이 항상 동일하게 유지되다'는 vary(다양하다, 달라지다)의 뜻과 반대이다. vary의 올바른 풀이는 'to be different or to change in different situations(상황에 따라 달라지거나 변하다)'이다. ② aggressive(공격적인): 타인을 향해 화가 나거나 폭력적인 방식으로 행동하는 ③ hungry(배고픈): 음식을 원하거나 필요로 하는 ④ control(통제하다): 어떤 것에 대한 힘을 갖고 무슨 일이 일어날지 결정하다 ⑤ recognize(인식하다): 전에 본 적 있는 사람이나 사물을 알아보고 기억하다

As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?

"You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. ⓒThat this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting ⓓannoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, ⓔhas become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
solution: ③ That → What 이 문장은 'this slogan means'의 목적어 역할을 하면서 동시에 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 한다. 접속사 That은 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끌며, 'that this slogan means'에서 'means'의 목적어가 없어 불완전한 구조가 된다. 따라서 명사절 내에서 목적어 역할을 동시에 수행하는 관계대명사 What으로 고쳐야 한다. ① 'we feel full, happy, and relaxed'에서 feel은 연결동사(linking verb)로 쓰여 형용사 보어를 취하고 있으므로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 주어 'hunger'가 3인칭 단수이므로 동사에 -(e)s를 붙인 sparks가 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 'get + 과거분사' 구문으로, 주어가 기분이 언짢아지는 수동적 상태가 되는 것이므로 과거분사 annoyed가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ '"hangry"라는 단어가 공식 영어 단어가 되었다'는 현재까지 완료된 결과를 나타내므로 현재완료 has become이 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to support that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.
solution: ③ 배고픔이 주의력과 자기통제력을 저하시킨다는 실험 결과를 종합하여 '식사 거르기가 주의력과 자기통제력을 약화시킨다'는 내용이 글 전체의 핵심이므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ① 'hangry'라는 단어가 도입부에 언급되지만, 글의 핵심은 배고픔과 분노의 조합 자체가 아니라 배고픔이 주의력과 자기통제력에 미치는 영향이다. ② Stroop 과제는 실험 결과를 뒷받침하는 하나의 사례일 뿐, 글 전체가 Stroop 과제를 다루는 것은 아니다. ④ 선택적 주의와 심적 회전은 실험에서 측정된 여러 과제 중 일부에 불과하며, 글의 주제를 이끌어내기 위한 세부 사항일 뿐 글 전체의 제목이 될 수 없다. ⑤ 학업 성취도를 높이는 식단 계획에 관한 내용은 지문에 전혀 언급되지 않았다.
choices: Hunger and Anger: A Dangerous Combination
The Stroop Task: A Window into Human Attention
How Skipping Meals Weakens Attention and Self- Control
Selective Attention and Mental Rotation in College Students
Diet Plans That Boost Academic Performance

Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. (B)이 슬로건이 의미하는 것은 배고픔이 여러분의 기분과 수행 능력을 실제로 바꿀 수 있다는 것이다. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)의 우리말과 일치하도록 <조건>에 따라 문장을 완성하시오.
조건 1. 문장의 주어는 관계대명사 what을 사용하여 명사절로 쓸 것
2. performance, seriously, slogan, means, hunger, mood를 포함할 것
3. 필요 시 단어를 추가하거나 형태를 변형할 것
→
answer: What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance.
solution: 이 슬로건이 의미하는 것'은 관계대명사 what을 사용하여 명사절 'What this slogan means'로 쓰고, 동사는 'is'를 쓴다. 뒤에는 '배고픔이 ~을 바꿀 수 있다는 것'이라는 보어절을 접속사 that을 생략한 형태로 이어 쓰되, 주어 'hunger'와 조동사 'can', 부사 'seriously', 동사 'change'를 순서대로 쓴다. 마지막으로 동사 change의 목적어로 'your mood'와 'performance'를 and로 연결하여 문장을 완성한다.

solution: (A)의 As는 '~함에 따라, ~하면서'라는 의미로, 수업이 진행됨에 따라 배고픔이 점차 커진다는 시간의 경과에 따른 동시 진행·비례를 나타내는 접속사이다. ⑤ 해가 짐에 따라 계곡의 기온이 급격히 떨어졌다는 의미로, 시간의 경과에 따라 두 상황이 함께 변화하는 비례의 접속사 As로 쓰였으므로 (A)와 의미가 같다. ① 완료된 상태(이미 사무실을 떠난 것)가 명백한 원인이 되어 결과(전화를 받지 못한 것)를 낳는 구조이므로, '~때문에'라는 이유를 나타낸다. ② '~로서'라는 의미의 자격·신분을 나타낸다. ③ '비록 ~이지만'이라는 의미의 양보를 나타내는 접속사로 쓰였다. ④ 'view A as B(A를 B로 여기다)' 구문에 쓰인 전치사 As이다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Some people seem to have a ⓐdeeply dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, ⓑwhich seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while ⓒothers are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don't like those foods. But wait, there's more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as ⓓwe are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors ⓔare linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains. We all seem to ⓕwire differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of ⓖwhich you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it's not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let's celebrate the fact ⓗthat we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
solution: ⓐ deeply dislike → deep dislike 'have' 뒤에서 관사 'a'의 수식을 받는 명사 dislike가 쓰였으므로, 명사를 수식하는 형용사 deep이 와야 한다. ⓔ are linked → linked 문장의 동사는 'are searching'이므로 중복해서 are를 쓸 수 없으며, 냄새와 '연결된다'는 수동의 의미를 나타내기 위해 과거분사의 형태로 receptors를 뒤에서 수식하는 구조가 되어야 한다. ⓕ wire → be wired 'wire'는 '~을 연결하다, 배선하다'라는 뜻의 타동사인데, 우리가 취향에 따라 서로 다르게 '만들어져 있다(타고나다)'는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 be wired로 고쳐야 한다. ⓖ which → whether '~인지 아닌지'라는 의미로 'like or dislike'라는 선택지를 나타내는 명사절 접속사가 필요하므로, 관계대명사 which가 아니라 whether로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 앞 내용을 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 which가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 앞서 언급된 'some people'과 대조되는 불특정 '다른 사람들'을 가리키는 대명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 주절의 동사가 be동사(is)이므로 뒤이어 비교되는 절에서도 이를 받는 대동사 are를 썼으며, "우리 자신이 독특한 것만큼 우리의 후각도 독특하다"라는 의미의 원급 비교 (as ~ as) 표현으로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓗ 'the fact'를 보충 설명하는 동격 접속사로 that이 바르게 쓰였다.

2개
3개
4개
5개

solution: ⓐ lately → late 'last night(어젯밤)'이라는 특정 과거 시점과 함께 '늦게까지'라는 의미가 되어야 한다. lately는 '최근에'라는 뜻으로 막연한 기간을 나타내며 특정 시점과는 함께 쓰이지 않으므로, '늦게'라는 뜻의 late로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ worst → worse '상황을 더 악화시키다'라는 뜻의 관용 표현은 두 상태를 비교하는 비교급이 쓰여야 한다. worst는 최상급이므로, 비교급 worse로 고쳐야 한다. ⓕ Embarrass → Embarrassed 제니가 당황함과 화남을 '느끼는' 대상이므로 과거분사가 쓰여야 하며, 뒤에 이어지는 형용사 angry와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 한다. 따라서 Embarrass를 과거분사 Embarrassed로 고쳐야 한다. ⓗ very → so 뒤에 결과의 that절이 이어지고 있으므로, '매우 ~해서 … 하다'라는 의미의 'so ~ that' 구문이 되어야 한다. ⓑ '버스를 타기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ tapping과 병렬 구조를 이루는 동명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ start의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. 다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 할 때, 밑줄 친 개념이 적용된 사례로 가장 적절한 것은?
Hunger and Psychology The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to support that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control. 3회차 실전 모의고사
solution: ⑤ 공복이 자제력을 낮추어 감정 조절을 어렵게 만든다는 지문의 핵심 내용을 정확히 반영한다. ① 지문은 과식이 아닌 공복이 인지 능력을 떨어뜨린다고 설명하므로 지문의 원리와 일치하지 않는다. ② 공복이 수행 능력을 저하시킨다는 실험 결과와 정반대되는 사례이므로 적절하지 않다. ③ 음식 섭취와 무관한 명상의 효과를 다루고 있어 지문의 개념과 관련이 없다. ④ 신체적 훈련의 성과를 보여줄 뿐 공복에 따른 심리적 변화를 나타내지 않는다.

A manager remains remarkably patient and calm during a stressful negotiation because they practiced meditation techniques right before the meeting started.
A mountain climber forgets to bring their safety gear but manages to reach the summit safely by relying on their intense physical training.
A designer who missed lunch to finish a project becomes easily irritated and yells at a teammate over a very minor formatting error.

solution: ④ 지문에서 단식 집단이 식사 집단보다 Stroop 과제에서 "더 많은 오류를 범했다"고 명시하고 있다. 즉 두 집단을 비교하는 기준은 응답 '속도'가 아니라 '정확성'이었으므로, 반응 속도를 기준으로 판단했다는 이 선택지는 지문 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ① 'hangry'라는 단어가 여러 국제 사전에서 공식 영어 단어로 등재되었다고 명시되어 있으므로 내용과 일치한다. ② 참가자들이 실험 직전 식사를 거르거나 푸짐한 식사를 하도록 요청받았다고 했으므로 글의 내용과 일치한다. ③ 실험 과제가 선택적 주의력뿐 아니라 정신적 회전, 쓰기, 좌절 관리까지 포함되었다고 언급되었다. ⑤ 결론에서 공복 상태가 주의력 감소와 자제력 저하 둘 다에 기여한다고 기술하고 있으며, 둘 사이에 우열이나 순위를 매기지 않았으므로 내용과 일치한다.
choices: "Hangry" has been officially listed in dictionaries across several countries.
Participants were split into two groups based on whether they had eaten.
The task range extended beyond attention skills to include frustration management.
Researchers judged Stroop performance by response speed rather than accuracy.
Both reduced attention span and self-control were linked to hunger, without either being ranked higher. 실전 모의고사 3회차

다음 글을 읽고, <조건>과 <보기>의 어구들을 참고하여 요 약문을 완성하시오.
You Are in Control Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.
조건 1. 보기의 모든 단어를 사용하되 필요하면 형태변 화 가능
2. if가 이끄는 부사절을 사용할 것

보기 can / they / hunger / Individuals / triggered / if / by / consciously / negative / regulate / states / their / emotions / recognize / emotion

answer: Individuals can regulate negative emotions triggered by hunger if they consciously recognize their emotional states.

body:
다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 <보기>의 상황을 분석했을 때, 가장 적절한 반응은?
Loneliness and Hunger While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
보기 Sarah recently moved to a new city for her job and has not yet made any friends.
On a Friday evening, she feels a deep sense of isolation while sitting alone in her quiet apartment. Although she ate a large meal only two hours ago, she suddenly finds herself browsing a food delivery app to order a large pizza and a tub of ice cream.
solution: ⑤ 사라는 친구가 없는 고립된 상황에서 느끼는 외로움을 달래기 위해 음식이라는 신체적 자극을 찾고 있으므로 지문의 원리에 부합한다. ① 사라의 배고픔은 영양소 결핍이라는 생물학적 욕구보다는 외로움이라는 감정에서 기인한 것이다. ② 본문에서 'hangry'는 신체적 욕구가 분노를 일으키는 것이지만, 사라는 외로움이 식욕을 유발한 것이므로 적절하지 않다. ③ 감정적 식사는 단기적인 완화책일 뿐 건강상의 위험 때문에 장기적인 해결책이 될 수 없다고 본문에 명시되어 있다. ④ 피자의 영양가에 집중하는 것은 정서적 허기로 인한 식욕 발생 원인과 직접적인 관련이 없다.
choices: Sarah's sudden hunger is primarily driven by her body's actual biological need for nutrients.
Sarah is demonstrating a "hangry" state where her anger is causing her physical hunger.
Ordering excessive food will serve as a healthy and sustainable long-term solution for her.
Her craving will likely disappear if she focuses on the nutritional value of the pizza.
Sarah is seeking physical nourishment as a way to cope with her emotional loneliness. 3회차 실전 모의고사

body:
다음 글의 내용을 재구성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(E)를 <조 건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
You're Just Hangry! "You're not you when you're hungry." Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?
<재구성> Due to her busy schedule, Jenny failed to have breakfast, which led to a (A) _____ in her patience during a challenging science class. As her hunger (B) _____ , she exhibited (C)
behaviors like tapping her pencil and snapping at her friends. This emotional (D) was triggered by her physiological state, making her feel (E) _____ in front of her classmates.
조건 1. <보기>의 표현만을 사용할 것 (중복 없음)
2. <보기>의 형태를 변형하지 말 것
보기 decline / intensified / proud / instability / decreased / stability / calm / increase / irritable / humiliated
(A)
(B)
(C)
(D)
(E)
solution: (A) 아침을 거른 뒤 과학 수업에서 인내심이 줄어들었으므로 'decline(감소)'이 가장 적절하다. (B) 수업이 계속될수록 배고픔이 심해졌으므로 'intensified(심해졌다)'가 가장 적절하다. (C) 연필을 두드리고 친구들에게 쏘아붙이는 행동을 수식하므로 'irritable(짜증을 내는)'이 가장 적절하다. (D) 공복 때문에 감정이 흔들린 상태이므로 'instability(불안정)'가 가장 적절하다. (E) 반 친구들이 배에서 나는 소리를 듣고 웃어 창피함을 느꼈으므로 'humiliated(굴욕감을 느낀)'가 가장 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies. 실전 모의고사 3회차
solution: ② 빈칸 앞에서 공복 상태일 때 혈중 포도당 수치가 떨어진다고 했고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 이것이 신체의 정상적인 기능에 대한 명백한 위협이라고 설명하고 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 포도당 감소가 세포에 미치는 부정적인 영향, 즉 세포가 제 기능을 수행하지 못하게 막는다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 'preventing cells'가 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다.
choices: supplying cells with extra energy
preventing cells
allowing the body to absorb nutrients
stimulating cells to produce hormones
encouraging cells to regulate temperature

ⓐdigest: to make food pass through your body and absorb it
ⓑcirculate: to stop moving and stay fixed in one place
ⓒrelease: to allow something to move freely or become available
ⓓcope: to deal with a difficult situation successfully
ⓔelevate: to raise something to a higher level or position
solution: ②가 정답이다. ② 제시된 풀이 '한 곳에 멈춰 고정되어 있다'는 circulate(순환하다)의 뜻과 정반대이다. circulate의 올바른 풀이는 'to move continuously around a place or system(한 장소나 시스템을 따라 계속해서 움직이다)'이다. ① digest(소화하다): 음식을 몸 안에서 분해하여 흡수하다 ③ release(방출하다): 무언가가 자유롭게 움직이거나 이용 가능하도록 내보내다 ④ cope(대처하다): 어려운 상황을 성공적으로 처리하다 ⑤ elevate(높이다): 무언가를 더 높은 수준이나 위치로 올리다 비상(홍) 3과 실전 모의고사 3회차

body:
다음 <보기>의 단어를 사용하여 밑줄 친 ⓐ 문장의 의미를 영어로 바꾸어 쓰시오.
Hunger and Psychology The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink.
ⓐConsequently, psychological studies seem to support that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.
조건 1. <보기>에 제시된 단어 중에서 선택하여 영작할 것 (총 12단어로 작성)
2. 'Research' 단어로 문장을 시작할 것
3. 'negatively influences' 구문을 사용할 것
보기 span / indicates / empty / attention / influences / that / support / lower / one's / and / hungry / contributes / stomach / Research / being / behavioral / concentration / negatively / restraint 연구는 배고픈 상태가 개인의 집중력과 행동 억제력에 부정적 인 영향을 미친다는 점을 나타낸다.
→
answer: Research indicates that being hungry negatively influences one's concentration and behavioral restraint.
solution: 'that'이 이끄는 명사절을 'indicates'의 목적어로 두고, 동명사구 'being hungry'를 절의 주어로 사용하였다. 'negatively influences' 뒤의 두 목적어를 'and'로 연결하여 총 12단어 조건을 충족한다.

body:

What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are _____ . Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry."
solution: ① 빈칸 앞에서 배고플 때 위협 및 부정적 감정과 관련된 뇌 영역의 활동이 증가한다고 했고, 빈칸이 포함된 절은 이와 대조적으로 자기 통제와 의사 결정 같은 고차원적 인지 능력을 담당하는 영역의 활동 패턴이 어떻게 되는지를 설명한다. 글 전체가 배고픔이 뇌 기능과 감정 조절을 부정적으로 교란한다는 논지를 일관되게 전개하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 고차원 인지 영역의 활동 패턴이 심각하게 변형·교란된다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 'greatly altered'가 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long- term solution due to health risks. Interestingly, the human brain's response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to , a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
solution: ③ 빈칸이 포함된 마지막 문장은 'Just as A, B'의 병렬 구조로, 신체적 영양 부족(A)의 결과와 사회적 영양 부족(B)의 결과를 대응시키고 있다. B절에서 사회적 영양 부족이 '사회적 굶주림'이라는 결핍 상태로 이어진다고 했으므로, 이와 대응되는 A절의 빈칸에는 신체적 영양 부족이 초래하는 부정적 내적 상태가 와야 한다. 또한 앞 단락에서 뇌가 외로움과 굶주림에 동일한 방식으로 반응한다고 했고, 'emotional eating'이 부정적 감정을 해소하려는 시도라고 설명했으므로, 신체적 영양 부족이 심리적 불쾌감을 유발함을 유추할 수 있다. 따라서 'psychological discomfort'이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다.

a sense of fullness

body:
다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 할 때, 밑줄 친 개념이 적용된 사례로 가장 적절한 것은?
I HATE Cucumbers Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don't like those foods.
solution: ⑤ 제인은 부모와 달리 특정 DNA를 물려받아 브로콜리의 쓴맛을 강하게 느끼며 이는 본문의 유전적 원리와 일치한다. ① 마크는 과거 식중독 경험 때문에 갑각류를 기피하며, 이는 유전이 아닌 심리적 요인에 의한 거부 반응이다. ② 사라는 환경 보호라는 개인적 신념에 따라 유기농을 선택한 것이므로 유전적 민감성과는 전혀 무관한 선택이다. ③ 데이비드는 반복적 노출을 통해 쓴맛에 적응한 사례로, 본문이 강조하는 선천적인 유전적 특성을 보여주지 않는다. ④ 클로이의 반응은 면역 체계의 이상인 알레르기 증상이며 특정 성분의 쓴맛을 감지하는 유전적 민감성이 아니다.
choices: Mark refuses to eat shellfish because he once experienced severe food poisoning after consuming undercooked shrimp at a seaside restaurant.

After drinking several cups of black coffee every morning for a year, David eventually learned to appreciate its complex and bold flavors.
Whenever Chloe eats peanuts, her skin breaks out in itchy hives and her throat starts to swell, requiring immediate medical attention.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don't like those foods. But wait, there's more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains. We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from . Thus, maybe it's not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let's celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.
solution: ③ 빈칸 앞에서는 맛 선호에 대해 사람마다 다르게 타고났다는 내용이 언급되고, 뒤에서는 이를 이유로 사람들을 탓하는 것이 적절하지 않다는 결론이 이어진다. 이는 앞서 1~2문단에서 설명한 쓴맛 민감성 유전자와 냄새 관련 유전자라는 근거를 종합하는 자리이므로, 취향의 차이가 단순한 선호를 넘어 'DNA 깊숙이 뿌리내린 생물학적 특성'에서 비롯된다는 ③이 흐름상 가장 적절하다.

an intentional effort to maintain a healthy lifestyle
biological programming rooted deep within our DNA
cultural backgrounds that dictate what is edible

While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment.
(A) Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
(B) That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
(C) Interestingly, the human brain's response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. 4회차 실전 모의고사
solution: 주어진 글은 '행그리(hangry)'와 반대 방향으로 작동하는 '외로운 허기' 현상을 소개하며, 고독감이 신체적 허기로 이어진다는 화제를 제시한다. (B)는 주어진 글의 '외로운 허기'를 'That is'로 받아 구체적으로 설명하며, 고독감을 느낄 때 허기를 느끼고 정서적 식사에서 위안을 찾지만 장기적으로는 좋지 않다는 내용으로 이어진다. (C)는 (B)에서 다룬 고독감과 허기의 관계를 '흥미롭게도 (Interestingly)'라는 표지로 이어받아, 뇌 영상 연구를 근거로 외로움과 허기가 뇌의 동일한 영역을 활성화한다는 과학적 근거를 제시한다. (A)는 (C)의 뇌 반응 유사성 연구를 '연구들도 또한(Studies also support)'으로 이어받아, 외로움이 허기와 유사한 신호로 기능하며 사회적 영양의 결핍이 사회적 허기로 이어진다는 결론으로 마무리한다. 따라서 (B)-(C)-(A)의 순서가 가장 적절하다.

You Are in Control Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. (A)What might be happening is you're just hangry.

Animal behavior provides a clear solution to human emotional instability.
Your negative mood may stem from physiological hunger rather than the immediate situation.

주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고 르시오.
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too.
(A) But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations.
(B) Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.
(C) When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance.
solution: 주어진 글은 배고픔과 분노의 관계를 심리학뿐 아니라 생리학에서도 다룬다고 소개하며, 신체 반응의 변화를 예고한다. (C)는 음식을 먹으면 포도당으로 분해되어 세포의 에너지원으로 흡수된다는 정상적인 생리 과정을 설명하며, 주어진 글의 '신체 반응'을 구체화한다. (A)는 역접의 연결어 'But'을 통해 (C)에서 설명한 정상적인 포도당 흡수 과정과 대조되는 상황, 즉 배고플 때 '포도당' 수치가 떨어져 위협이 되고 신체가 '코르티솔'을 분비해 대응한다는 내용으로 이어진다. (B)는 (A)에서 언급된 '코르티솔'이 상승했을 때 나타나는 심박수, 혈압 증가와 불안, 짜증, 우울 등 심리적 효과를 설명하며 마무리한다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 자연스럽다.
choices: (C) ‒ (B) ‒ (A) 4회차 실전 모의고사

pathway, suggesting they are biologically comparable. Both states operate as (B) mechanisms designed to alert an individual to a particular (C) _____ . While hunger points to a need for food, loneliness indicates a lack of social (D) _____ . Ultimately, these feelings create a state of (E) that compels the individual to seek what is missing for their well-being.

solution: (A) 외로움과 배고픔이 뇌의 같은 영역에서 처리되므로 'neural(신경의)'이 가장 적절하다. (B) 두 상태 모두 부족함을 알리는 역할을 하므로 'signaling(신호를 보내는)'이 가장 적절하다. (C) 해결해야 할 결핍을 가리키므로 'deficit(결핍)'이 가장 적절하다. (D) 인간관계의 부족을 음식에 빗대어 표현하므로 'nourishment(영양)'가 가장 적절하다. (E) 결핍이 심리적 불편함을 일으키므로 'discomfort(불편함)'가 가장 적절하다.

What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry."

The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers ⓐconducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked ⓑto either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at
ⓒvarying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, ⓓin which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to support that an empty stomach ⓔcontribute to lower attention span and self-control.

But wait, there's more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are ⓐsensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors,
ⓑcreating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors
ⓒlinked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains. We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management ⓐwas recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, ⓑin which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, ⓓpreventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone ⓔwhat helps our body cope with stressful situations. No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely ⓓlinked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when ⓔdepriving of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Everybody knows that regular exercise improves mood, and doctors often mention the sense of calm, the relief ⓐwhat physical activity brings after a stressful day. Many adults who jog every morning before work ⓑreport feeling more focused throughout the day. It is certainly true that people who never move their bodies often feel sluggish and unmotivated, a state many call "couch fatigue." But people who spend most of their time indoors, away from parks ⓒwhere they could walk or stretch, lose a lot more than fitness. This is especially true ⓓduring the winter months, when outdoor activity naturally decreases. Doctors say ⓔthat people who stop exercising gradually lose energy, confidence, and the resilience that active bodies build. Of course, yoga, cycling, or even a short walk outside can help lift one's spirits. But in the long run, we need to design communities that support active living for everyone.
solution: ①ⓐ이 정답이다. 앞에 선행사 'the relief'가 있으므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 'what'을 쓸 수 없다. 목적격 관계대명사 'that[which]'으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 주어 'Many adults who jog every morning before work'가 복수이므로 복수동사 'report'가 올바르다. ⓒ 'where'는 장소를 나타내는 선행사 'parks'를 수식하는 관계부사로 올바르다. ⓓ 'during'은 뒤의 명사구 'the winter months'와 함께 특정 기간을 나타내는 전치사로 올바르다. ⓔ 'that'은 'say'의 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 올바르다.

Sleep experts say that this daytime fatigue is caused by a lack of deep sleep, the restorative rest ⓑwhat growing brains need most. It is certainly true that students who stay awake all night before exams often struggle to concentrate the following day, a problem many call "exam brain fog." But people who stay glued to screens ⓒduring the late hours of the night lose a lot more than rest. They may lose their link to focus, memory, and clear thinking, and many experts warn ⓓthat long-term sleep loss can hurt overall health. Of course, taking short naps, exercising, or reading before bed can help restore some energy. But in the long run, we need to build better daily habits. We need to create routines ⓔwhere students can get the rest, balance, and focus that growing minds require.
solution: ②ⓑ가 정답이다. 앞에 선행사 'the restorative rest'가 있으므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 'what'을 쓸 수 없다. 목적격 관계대명사 'that[which]'으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 주어 'most teenagers who stay up late texting or gaming'이 복수이므로 복수동사 'show'가 올바르다. ⓒ 'during'은 뒤의 명사구 'the late hours of the night'과 함께 특정 기간 동안이라는 의미를 나타내는 전치사로 올바르다. ⓓ 'that'은 'warn'의 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓔ 'where'는 선행사 'routines'를 받아 그 안에서 학생들이 충분한 휴식을 취할 수 있다는 의미를 나타내는 관계부사로 올바르다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

The focus itself is tied to the space ⓑin which you study. As long as you remain in a cluttered space, you're likely to stay ⓒdistracted. Removing yourself from that space prevents your mind from
ⓓwandering away. To take the first step, try separating ⓔyourself from the source of distraction.
solution: ⓐ that은 선행사 없이 명사절을 이끄는 용법으로 쓰일 수 없으므로, '~하는 것'이라는 의미로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what으로 고쳐야 한다. → figure out that is distracting them은 figure out what is distracting them으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ in which는 선행사 the space를 받는 관계대명사로 전치사 in의 목적어 역할을 하며 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 올바르다. ⓒ stay는 상태를 나타내는 연결동사로 뒤에 형용사 보어 distracted가 오는 것이 올바르다. ⓓ prevent A from B(~ing) 구문에서 동명사 wandering이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ separate의 목적어가 주어 you와 동일 대상을 가리키므로 재귀대명사 yourself가 올바르게 쓰였다.
