body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Choosing a travel destination is about much more than distance or cost. Humans pick destinations and travel packages based on how we expect (A)
[it / them] to feel and appear in our photos, not to mention the sense of excitement our hearts will register as a reward for choosing somewhere thrilling. Cost is rarely the most important factor on our minds when we plan our trip. More often it's the atmosphere, the culture, the memory attached to visiting the same place (B)[that / what] your family visited every summer when you were young. All these conscious, subconscious, and nearly nostalgic thoughts and emotions (C)[flood / flooding] the mind in a matter of moments, and you make a booking.
solution: (A)는 앞에 나온 복수 명사 destinations and travel packages를 가리키므로 복수 대명사 them이 와야 한다. (B)는 앞에 선행사 place가 있으므로 선행사를 필요로 하는 관계대명사 that이 적절하며, 선행사가 필요 없는 what은 쓸 수 없다. (C)는 문장의 주어인 복수 명사 thoughts and emotions에 대한 본동사가 필요하므로 동사 원형 flood가 와야 하며, flooding은 준동사이므로 본동사 역할을 할 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 ① them - that - flood이다.
choices: them - that - flood
it - what - flooding
them - what - flood
it - that - flooding
it - what - flood

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Why do we clench our fists during the highly intense, dramatically staged final minutes of certain sports matches? Because mirror neurons in our brains recreate for us the tension (A)[that / what] we see on the field. We have empathy for the athletes - we know how they're feeling - because we literally experience the same feelings ourselves. And when we watch the players celebrate on the field? Some of the cells firing in our brain are the same ones that (B)[fire / firing] when we celebrate our own victories. 'Vicarious' is not a strong enough word to describe the effect of these mirror neurons. When we see someone else struggling or exhausted, mirror neurons help us to sense her or his physical strain and actually
(C)[make / making] us feel the struggle or the exhaustion of the other person. These moments are the foundation of empathy and possibly of solidarity, a solidarity that is deeply rooted in our biology. * mirror neuron: 거울 신경 세포 ** vicarious: 대리의, 간접적인
solution: (A) 'the tension'이라는 선행사가 존재하므로 관계대명사 that이 필요하며, 선행사가 없을 때 쓰는 what은 올 수 없다. (B) that은 'the same ones(=cells)'를 가리키는 주격 관계대명사이므로 뒤에는 수와 시제가 일치하는 정동사가 와야 한다. 분사형 firing은 문장 구조상 적절하지 않으므로 fire가 와야 한다. (C) 'help us to sense ~ and actually (to) make ~' 구조에서 앞의 to sense와 병렬을 이루기 위해 to가 생략된 원형부정사 make가 적절하며, making은 병렬 구조를 깨뜨린다. 따라서 정답은 ② that - fire - make이다.
choices: what - fire - make _____
that - fire - make
that - firing - make
that - fire - making
what - firing - making

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
ⓐJudged by wingspan alone, the albatross has the widest wingspan among all living birds, extending up to 3.5 meters. This span is nearly twice that of the largest eagle species. Much of this remarkable span is ⓑdue to elongated bone structures that reduce the energy needed for gliding. The albatross is not the only bird built for efficient flight, though. Hummingbirds, despite their tiny size, are remarkably skilled fliers as well. Unlike gliders, hummingbirds have wings built in a highly compact form that allows ⓒextremely rapid wingbeats exceeding fifty times per second. Despite its length, the albatross's wing bone structure ⓓis far lighter than expected. Among flying birds, the albatross's efficient bone structure makes long-distance travel possible with minimal effort. Most of the lift they generate comes from the specialized feather arrangement
ⓔwhat is found only along the outer edge of each wing.
solution: ⑤는 명사 'the specialized feather arrangement'를 선행사로 받는 관계사 자리인데, 'what'은 선행사를 취할 수 없는 관계대명사이므로 어법상 틀리다. 'what' 대신 'that' 또는 'which'를 써야 한다. ① 'Judged'는 '~로 판단하면'이라는 뜻의 분사구문으로 문두에서 부사적으로 쓰여 어법상 옳다. ② 'due to'는 명사(구) 앞에서 '~때문에'라는 뜻으로 쓰이는 전치사구로 어법상 옳다. ③ 'extremely rapid'는 부사 'extremely'가 형용사 'rapid'를 수식하여 뒤의 명사 'wingbeats'를 꾸며주는 구조로 어법상 옳다. ④ 주어 'the albatross's wing bone structure'가 단수이므로 단수 동사 'is'가 쓰인 것은 어법상 옳다.

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
It is important that managers, HR specialists, trainers, executives and occasionally even shareholders appreciate (A)[that / what] feedback is the starting point for the improvement of many workplace training programs. Other inputs, or investments, include items such as time, materials, funding, technology and administrative support. Many of these inputs depend directly or indirectly on qualified trainers, and it is increasingly vital that none of these important or valuable inputs (B)[is / to be] wasted as a result of poor planning. In addition to the inputs listed above, there is competition for funding for other purposes, including expansion, development of new products and demands from other departments. It is therefore imperative that the training material
(C)[preparing / prepared] is of the best possible quality, regardless of the proportionate cost of materials to all other inputs.
solution: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 절 'feedback is the starting point for the improvement of many workplace training programs'는 주어, 동사, 보어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이므로 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사 that이 적절하다. what은 불완전한 절을 이끌어야 하므로 적절하지 않다. (B) that절의 주어인 'none of these important or valuable inputs'에 대한 본동사가 필요하므로 정동사 is가 적절하다. to be는 준동사로 본동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로 적절하지 않다. (C) 교육 자료는 '준비되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 prepared가 명사 training material을 수식하는 것이 적절하다. 현재분사 preparing은 능동의 의미를 나타내므로 문맥상 적절하지 않다. 따라서 정답은 ④ that - is - prepared이다.
choices: that - is - preparing
that - to be - prepared
what - is - prepared
that - is - prepared
what - to be - preparing

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Most of what we do during a daily commute we are not consciously aware of ⓐit, unless something unusual happens along the way. This automatic response is possible because of habitual memory, the part of us ⓑthat runs in the background, similar to a program running while we work on something else. This does not mean, however, ⓒthat if a task is normally handled by habitual memory, we cannot manage it with conscious effort. For example, checking mirrors while driving is often automatic: it happens quickly and without much thought once we have practiced enough. Yet it is also something we can consciously control. You can slow down your reactions, glance at each mirror in turn, and then
ⓓsignal clearly before changing lanes. Drivers often turn an automatic habit into a deliberate safety check. There are moments ⓔwhen you may already do this on a conscious level, such as when you drive through a busy intersection. * habitual memory: 습관 기억(반복적 행동을 통해 형성되는 무 의식적 기억)
solution: 정답은 ①이다. 'Most of what we do during a daily commute'가 이미 문두로 나와 'aware of'의 목적어 역할을 하고 있으므로, 뒤에서 대명사 it으로 다시 지칭하면 중복 지칭이 되어 어법상 틀리다. it을 삭제해야 올바른 문장이 된다. ② that은 선행사 'the part of us'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ that은 동사 mean의 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사로 올바르다. ④ signal은 앞의 slow down, glance와 병렬 구조를 이루는 동사원형으로 올바르다. ⑤ when은 선행사 moments를 수식하는 관계부사로 올바르게 쓰였다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Schools in regions with growing access to technology developed appropriate programs to teach and guide students in using digital devices safely. These included measures to avoid careless sharing of information; the adoption of curricula appropriate to the prevailing conditions, making effective use of online tools for learning and other productive activities, and the establishment of institutional and administrative guidelines (A)[that / what] largely influenced the behavior of teachers and students. These efforts to manage limited resources and training also included measures and strategies to cope with situations when incidents aggravated existing concerns about safety. In the schools that succeeded, the present systems correspond to an integration of a strong educational tradition with modern technology, pedagogy, social and administrative practice (B)
[respond / to respond] to the challenges of digital change. In part due to the rapidity of recent technological growth, this integration is not entirely satisfactory due to the conflicting demands of innovation, and thus creative thinking is required to make digital education (C)
[sustainable / sustainably].
solution: (A)에는 선행사 'institutional and administrative guidelines'가 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. what은 선행사가 없을 때 사용하는 관계대명사이므로 이 문맥에서는 부적절하다. (B)에는 명사 'practice'를 수식하며 목적을 나타내는 to부정사가 와야 하므로 to respond가 적절하다. respond는 정형동사 형태로 문장 구조상 맞지 않는다. (C)에는 'make + 목적어 + 목적격보어' 구조에서 형용사 보어가 와야 하므로 sustainable이 적절하다. 부사 sustainably는 목적격보어로 쓰일 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
choices: that - respond - sustainably
what - respond - sustainable
what - to respond - sustainable
that - to respond - sustainably
that - to respond - sustainable

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
With the constant flow of new studies published, public conversations about nutrition have been growing in recent years, even though there is evidence ⓐwhat media and public interest in the topic waxes and wanes. Articles about and reports on unhealthy diets, obesity, and food additives ⓑhave become more frequent, as journals have expanded discussions about the science, policy, and industry implications surrounding nutrition. Importantly, there are differences in how sources locally and around the world present nutritional information, with some providing more and clearer data and others focusing on topics ⓒwhich may or may not be useful to the public's understanding of the issue. Even researchers working at health institutes may have different perceptions of their capacity ⓓto convey the message about such dietary problems as malnutrition. Overall, though, it's evident that journals and other communicators aren't doing a great job of educating us about nutrition ⓔso that we truly understand why we need to change our eating habits.
solution: ① what은 선행사 없이 쓰이는 관계사/의문사로, evidence 뒤에서 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 자리에는 쓰일 수 없다. that으로 고쳐야 한다. ② 주어가 복수(Articles ... and reports ...)이므로 복수동사 have become은 올바른 수 일치이다. ③ 선행사 topics를 받는 주격 관계대명사 which는 적절하다. ④ capacity to R 형태로 명사를 수식하는 to부정사는 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ so that은 완전한 절을 이끄는 목적의 부사절 접속사로 적절하다.

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Icons have high quantitative representation in sports magazines and broadcasts, as well as in books on athletics, photojournalism, and cultural analysis. By one count, for example, the photograph of the 'player celebrating the winning goal' during the championship match in 2002 (A)
[have / has] appeared more than ten thousand times in different sports media publications. In contrast, the vast majority of each season's game images make brief or limited appearances and are quickly replaced. In addition, icons have another property (B)[imposing / imposed] on them that is connected with repetition: 'signature shots' are typically front-page, lead-of-the-broadcast items that eventually show up on the covers of sports or historical works. This environmental context reinforces and confirms the icons' status as memorable. People are more likely to pay attention to and remember moments (C)[that / what] are more prominently displayed in the sports media stream; sports commentators (analysts and journalists) are more likely to pick up on such images as being worthy of discussion and fan attention.
solution: (A)의 주어는 the photograph of the 'player celebrating the winning goal'이며 핵심 주어 the photograph이 단수이므로 has가 적절하다. (B)는 property와 impose가 수동 관계이므로 ‘부여된’ 이라는 뜻의 과거분사 imposed가 적절하다. (C)는 앞의 선행사 moments를 수식하고 are more prominently displayed의 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사가 필요하므로 that이 적절하다. 선행사를 포함하는 what은 이미 선행사 moments가 있으므로 사용할 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 ②이다.
choices: have - imposing - that
has - imposed - that
have - imposed - what
has - imposing - that
has - imposed - what

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
If you memorize only a few words each day, you can't expect to become fluent in a language. It's very simple. You get out what you put in. The same is true in most areas of our lives. Steve Jobs, Elon Musk, and Bill Gates, to name a few, are brilliant entrepreneurs, but they each worked hard ⓐto build their companies from scratch. And if you are one of those fortunate enough to be more gifted than others, you will eventually learn
ⓑwhat raw talent cannot replace years of practice. If you have a skill that you take for granted and don't continue to develop ⓒit, you will gradually lose it. If you don't review your notes, practice speaking, and ⓓcomplete your exercises every day, don't expect to master a new language. The more consistently you practice, ⓔthe faster you will improve.
solution: ②의 what은 뒤에 완전한 절(raw talent cannot replace years of practice)이 이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 한다. ①의 to build는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사의 부사적 용법으로 적절하다. ③의 it은 앞에 나온 skill을 가리키는 목적격 대명사로 적절하다. ④의 complete는 review, practice와 병렬을 이루는 동사원형으로 적절하다. ⑤의 the faster는 'the 비교급, the 비교급' 구문으로 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Scientific evidence shows that ⓐwhich we choose in everyday situations is largely guided by unconscious biases, not by careful reasoning. Decisions are your brain's quick estimations of the best available option. In every choice, you're faced with limited time and incomplete information from your environment. Your brain uses past outcomes to generate a preference - the decision - and compares ⓑit to the incoming information about the current situation. In this manner, decision-making lets your brain narrow down alternatives, functioning as a tool not only for choosing but also for ⓒevaluating risks, forming preferences, and many other cognitive activities. Our common sense might declare that choosing, judging, and evaluating ⓓare different mental events, yet one general process describes them all. Decision-making is the default mode for practical reasoning. It also holds a key to
ⓔunlocking the mystery of how the brain balances risk and reward.
solution: 정답은 ①이다. 'which'는 선행사가 없는 명사절을 이끌 수 없으므로, 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'이라는 의미의 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사 'what'으로 고쳐야 한다. ② it은 앞서 언급된 'the decision'을 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다. ③ evaluating은 전치사 for의 목적어로 choosing과 병렬 구조를 이루는 동명사이므로 적절하다. ④ are는 choosing, judging, evaluating이라는 복수의 동명사구 주어에 수를 일치시킨 동사이므로 적절하다. ⑤ unlocking은 전치사 to 뒤에 오는 동명사로 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Basic artistic talent is often inherited; its full expression in a person's life ⓐdoes not. Even very young children can show early signs of artistic interest, such as drawing or singing spontaneously. But specific styles like 'abstract painting' and 'improvisational jazz' are not
ⓑinnately programmed. Your appreciation for a particular art form develops only because you grew up in a setting ⓒwhere that art form was practiced and celebrated regularly, and your mind absorbs its patterns unconsciously to shape your creative choices. What's clear is ⓓthat you'll develop certain preferences for creative expression because your brain forms connections based on repeated exposure and practice. Even skilled artists continue to refine these preferences throughout their careers. The techniques you learn and apply ⓔare shaped by both formal training and personal experimentation.
solution: ①의 does not는 앞 문장 'is often inherited'라는 be동사 구문과 병치를 이루는 생략 구문이므로, do동사가 아니라 be동사 형태인 is not이 되어야 한다(주어 expression은 단수이므로 is not). 따라서 ①이 어법상 틀린 부분이다. ② innately는 분사 programmed를 수식하는 부사로 적절하다. ③ where는 구체적 상황을 나타내는 setting을 선행사로 하는 관계부사로 올바르다. ④의 that은 be동사 is의 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 적절하다. ⑤는 복수 주어 techniques에 맞는 수 일치이므로 are는 올바르다.

body:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 어법상 틀린 것을 찾아 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
Medical science ⓐhas made tremendous progress in recent decades. Doctors in earlier times did not possess the knowledge and equipment that modern physicians ⓑare now, making disease treatment ⓒfar more difficult and uncertain. Currently, healthcare is more effective, precise, and widely ⓓavailable. *make tremendous progress 엄청난 진보를 이루다 ( ),
solution: ⓑ동사 'possess'를 대신하는 대동사 'do'로 고쳐야 한다. 앞 문장의 'possess the knowledge and equipment'에서 'possess'를 반복하지 않고 'do'로 대체한 것으로 '가지고 있다'를 의미한다.

body: 다음 중 문법에 맞지 않는 문장을 고르시오.
solution: teachers study at night'에서 주절과 공통되는 부분인 'study at night'을 생략하거나 대동사 'do'로 표현해야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전
choices: This is the worst movie I have ever watched.
Students study much harder at night than teachers are.
The policy covers not more than three accidents per year.
The building collapsed a few minutes after the earthquake.
Senior citizens are respected even more deeply than young people.

body: 다음 중 문법에 맞지 않는 문장을 고르시오.
solution: adults play at the playground'에서 주절과 공통되는 부분인 'play at the playground'를 생략하거나 대동사 'do'로 표현해야 한다.
choices: She is the smartest student I have ever taught.
The warranty covers not more than two years for the device.
Children play much longer at the playground than adults are.
The car broke down just moments before reaching the destination.
Foreign visitors are welcomed even more warmly than locals.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법과 문맥상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
Tom always has his guitar nearby; he ⓐis used to playing whenever he has free time. He says he never loses interest in music. His love for playing guitar ⓑcould be uplifting. He ⓒhas taught some of his favorite songs and chords to his neighbors. He ⓓwould like to spend more time practicing music. So he wants to join a band and so ⓔare his neighbors. *uplifting 행복감을 주는
solution: ⑤ⓔ are → do 앞 문장의 일반동사를 대신할 때는 be동사가 아닌 대동사 do를 사용한다. 주어인 his neighbors에 맞추어 변경한다. ⓐ 자유 시간이 있을 때마다 기타를 연주하는 것에 익숙하다는 의미로 is used to playing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓑ 가능성을 나타내는 조동사 could가 동사원형 be와 함께 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 과거부터 지금까지 이웃들에게 노래와 코드를 가르쳐 왔다는 현재완료 시제 has taught가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 음악을 연습하며 더 많은 시간을 보내고 싶다는 소망을 나타내는 would like to가 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
(A), (B), (C)에 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
I visited a restaurant (A) [whose / whom] chef was Italian. The food there was much better than I had imagined. The waiter was from Spain and spoke English with a strong accent. So whenever he explained the menu, I couldn't understand (B)
[what / that] he was recommending. But it was one of the few places (C) [which / whose] I frequently visited during my stay in Barcelona.
solution: (A): chef와의 소유 관계를 나타내는 말이 필요하므로 관계대명사 whose가 알맞다. (B): ‘그가 추천한 것’이라는 의미를 포함한 명사절이 필요하므로 what이 적절하다. (C): 선행사 places를 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사가 와야 하므로 which가 맞다.
choices: whose - what - whose
whose - what - which
whose - that - which
whom - that - whose
whom - what - whose

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Psychology is not the only field of science
ⓐconcerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and ⓑgets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry,
ⓒpreventing cells from performing ⓓwhat they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels ⓔleads to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.
solution: ⓔ 주어 'Elevated cortisol levels'가 복수이므로 동사원형 'lead'를 써야 한다. ⓐ 'concerned'는 과학 분야가 특정 관계와 관련된 수동 의미를 나타내는 과거분사이므로 적절하다. ⓑ 'gets absorbed'는 포도당이 세포에 흡수되는 수동 관계를 나타내므로 적절하다. ⓒ 'preventing'은 앞 절의 결과를 부연하는 분사구문이므로 적절하다. ⓓ 'what'은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로 'do'의 목적어 역할을 하므로 적절하다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers ⓐconducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked ⓑto either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at ⓒvarying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, ⓓin which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to support that an empty stomach ⓔcontribute to lower attention span and self-control.
solution: ⓔ 주어 'an empty stomach'가 3인칭 단수이므로 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙여야 한다. ⓐ 'conducted'는 연구자들이 실험을 수행한 능동 관계의 과거형 동사이므로 적절하다. ⓑ 'to either skip'은 'were asked' 뒤에서 요구된 행동을 나타내는 to부정사이고 'skip'과 'eat'을 병렬로 연결하므로 적절하다. ⓒ 'varying'은 서로 다른 난도를 나타내며 명사 'levels'를 수식하므로 적절하다. ⓓ 'in which'는 스트룹 과제라는 상황을 선행사로 받고 뒤의 완전한 절을 이끄므로 적절하다.

Jenny was up ⓐlately last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush ⓑto catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters ⓒworst because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and ⓓshooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start
ⓔnoticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. ⓕEmbarrass and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? 실전 학습 After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. ⓖWhat this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is ⓗvery common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. solution: ⓐ lately → late 'last night(어젯밤)'이라는 특정 과거 시점과 함께 '늦게까지'라는 의미가 되어야 한다. lately는 '최근에'라는 뜻으로 막연한 기간을 나타내며 특정 시점과는 함께 쓰이지 않으므로, '늦게'라는 뜻의 late로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ worst → worse '상황을 더 악화시키다'라는 뜻의 관용 표현은 두 상태를 비교하는 비교급이 쓰여야 한다. worst는 최상급이므로, 비교급 worse로 고쳐야 한다. ⓕ Embarrass → Embarrassed 제니가 당황함과 화남을 '느끼는' 대상이므로 과거분사가 쓰여야 하며, 뒤에 이어지는 형용사 angry와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 한다. 따라서 Embarrass를 과거분사 Embarrassed로 고쳐야 한다. ⓗ very → so 뒤에 결과의 that절이 이어지고 있으므로, '매우 ~해서 … 하다'라는 의미의 'so ~ that' 구문이 되어야 한다. ⓑ '버스를 타기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ tapping과 병렬 구조를 이루는 동명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ start의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. (start는 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취할 수 있음) ⓖ 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사 What이 올바르게 쓰였다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 같도록 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. (A)이 슬로 건이 의미하는 것은 배고픔이 당신의 기분과 행동을 심각하 게 바꿀 수 있다는 것이다. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
조건 1. 관계대명사 what을 사용할 것
2. <보기>의 단어들을 모두 사용할 것(어형 변화가능)
3. 총 13단어
보기 mean / be / this slogan / can / hunger / your mood / seriously change / and / performance
(A)
answer: (A): What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance.
solution: 관계대명사 what을 사용하여 'What + 주어 + 동사' 형태의 명사절을 만들고, 이를 문장의 주어로 사용한다. 뒤에는 is를 써서 주어를 보충 설명하며, hunger can seriously change your mood and performance가 슬로건의 의미를 나타내는 보어 역할을 한다. 따라서 'What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance.'라고 영작한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger ⓐcaused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often ⓑlooking for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way ⓒto relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long- term solution due to health risks. Interestingly, the human brain's response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown ⓓwhat the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, ⓔindicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
solution: ④ what → that "brain imaging studies have shown what the same area in the brain is turned on..."에서 show의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 자리이다. 뒤에 오는 절 "the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings"는 주어와 동사가 모두 갖춰진 완전한 절이므로, 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what이 아니라 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that을 써야 한다. 따라서 ④가 정답이다. ① "caused by"는 앞의 명사 "emotional feelings of anger"를 수식하는 과거분사구로, 감정이 신체적 필요에 의해 '유발되는' 수동의 의미가 적절하게 쓰였다. ② "looking for"는 앞 절의 주어 "some people"을 의미상 주어로 하는 분사구문으로, 능동의 의미가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ "a good way to relieve"에서 to relieve는 명사 way를 수식하는 to부정사의 형용사적 용법으로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ "indicating"은 앞 절 전체를 의미상 주어로 하는 분사구문으로, 능동의 의미가 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals ⓐvary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when ⓑdepriving of food, and schooling fish exhibit ⓒreduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able ⓓto recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you ⓔskipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.
solution: ② depriving of → deprived of 'fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food'에서 fruit flies는 먹이를 빼앗기는 대상, 즉 수동의 의미를 가진다. 따라서 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 depriving이 아니라 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 deprived를 써야 한다. 'when deprived of food'는 'when they are deprived of food'에서 접속사 when 뒤의 주어와 be동사가 생략된 분사구문이다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ① Individuals가 복수 주어이므로 복수 동사 vary가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ reduced는 과거분사로 명사 group unity를 수식하는 형용사 역할을 하며, '감소된 집단 결속력'이라는 수동의 의미를 올바르게 나타낸다. ④ 'be able to + 동사원형' 구조에서 to recognize는 to부정사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 'if you skipped lunch'에서 과거에 점심을 거른 사실을 묻는 것이므로 과거 시제 skipped가 올바르게 쓰였다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter ⓐthat helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in ⓑmaintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show ⓒwhat, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas
ⓓresponsible for higher cognitive skills like self- control and decision-making are greatly
ⓔaltered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry."
solution: ③ what → that show 뒤에 이어지는 절 "when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity"는 주어(areas)와 동사(increase)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이다. 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what은 쓸 수 없으며, 완전한 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that을 써야 한다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ① 선행사 'a neurotransmitter'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that이 올바르게 쓰였다. 선행사가 사물이므로 that의 사용이 적절하며, 뒤에 동사 helps가 이어져 주격 역할을 바르게 수행하고 있다. ② 전치사 in의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사 maintaining이 올바르게 쓰였다. 'play a crucial role in -ing' 구조에서 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다. ④ 'areas responsible for higher cognitive skills'에서 responsible for는 형용사구로 명사 areas를 후치수식하고 있다. 'be responsible for(~을 담당하다)'의 의미로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 'the activity patterns ... are greatly altered'에서 altered는 동사 are와 함께 수동태를 이루고 있다. activity patterns가 '변화되는' 대상이므로 과거분사 altered가 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
Psychology is not the only field of science
ⓐconcerning with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy
ⓑrequired for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are
ⓒsupposing to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat ⓓby released cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions ⓔseems to be in line with psychological studies.
solution: ② 'the energy required for their proper performance'에서 required는 앞의 명사 energy를 수식하는 과거분사로, '그들의 적절한 수행에 필요한 에너지'라는 수동의 의미를 나타낸다. energy가 require의 동작을 받는 대상이므로 과거분사 required가 올바르게 쓰였다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ① concerning → concerned 'field of science'가 '~와 관련된'이라는 수동·상태의 의미로 수식되어야 하므로, 현재분사 concerning이 아닌 과거분사 concerned가 와야 한다. 'be concerned with(~에 관심을 갖다/관련되다)'의 수동 형태가 명사를 후치 수식하는 구조이므로 concerned가 옳다. ③ supposing → supposed 'be supposed to do'는 '~하기로 되어 있다'는 의미의 고정 표현으로, 과거분사 supposed가 와야 한다. supposing은 '~라고 가정하면'이라는 분사구문·접속사로 쓰이는 형태로 이 문맥에 맞지 않는다. ④ by released → by releasing 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(releasing)가 와야 한다. 과거분사 released는 전치사의 목적어로 쓰일 수 없으므로 by releasing으로 고쳐야 한다. ⑤ seems to → seem to 주어 'These physiological reactions'가 복수이므로 동사도 복수형인 seem이 와야 한다. 단수 동사형 seems는 복수 주어와 수 일치가 되지 않으므로 틀렸다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. ⓔElevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

Hunger and the Brain What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. ⓐSerotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. ⓑWhen serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is preserved, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. ⓒThese images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions decrease in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self- control and decision-making are greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry." You Are in Control Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. ⓓIndividuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: ⓔPeople seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry.

ⓐWhile being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for a comfort in excessive "emotional eating." ⓑEmotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks. Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can.
(A) For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. .
(B) This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight.
(C) In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information. 1회차 실전 모의고사

(C)는 'In fact, she can open up'에서 'she'가 (A)의 학생을 가리키며, 그 학생이 검증하고자 하는 정보의 유형을 확장하고 과학 저널 같은 일차 출처까지 활용할 수 있음을 덧붙여 마무리한다. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C)의 순서가 가장 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed , making it necessary to change reading strategies.

body:
밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.
solution: ① 밑줄 친 'change reading strategies'는 읽기 전략을 바꾸어야 한다는 뜻으로, 밑줄 앞에서 수직적 읽기는 텍스트 하나에만 의존해 저자의 신뢰성, 논리, 참고문헌을 평가하는 방식이었다고 했고, 기술이 글을 쓰고 출판하는 환경을 변화시켰다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 밑줄 친 부분에는 '텍스트 내부 근거에만 의존하는 평가 방식을 넘어서야 한다'는 의미가 와야 자연스럽다. 따라서 ①이 정답이다.
choices: move beyond evaluating texts using only internal evidence
rely more heavily on an author's spoken credibility
replace vertical reading with checking the publisher alone
limit analysis to the references cited within a single book
abandon critical evaluation skills developed for print media

body:
밑줄 친 우리말 문장을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. 예를 들어, 책을 읽고 나서, 독자는 본문에 제시된 주장들이 충분한 증거에 의해 뒷받침되는지를 검토할 수 있다. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.
조건 1. 분사구문과 관계대명사를 모두 사용할 것
2. (read, a book, a reader, review, argument, present, support, enough evidence)를 모두 포함할 것
3. 필요 시 어형을 변형할 것
4. 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것
→
answer: Having read a book, a reader can review if the arguments that are presented in the text are supported by enough evidence.
solution: 정답 문장은 분사구문과 관계대명사가 결합된 복합 구문으로 구성된다. 먼저, '책을 읽고 나서'는 완료 분사구문 'Having read a book'으로 표현한다. 'read'를 'Having read'로 어형 변형하여 분사구문을 만든다. 다음으로, '본문에 제시된 주장들'은 관계대명사 'that'을 사용하여 'the arguments that are presented in the text'로 표현한다. 'present'는 수동의 의미를 나타내기 위해 'presented'로 변형하고, 관계대명사 'that'은 박스에 없으므로 학생이 스스로 추가해야 한다. '뒷받침되는지'는 수동태 'are supported by'로 표현하며, 'support'를 'supported'로 변형한다. 'argument'는 복수형 'arguments'로, 'review'는 'can review'의 형태로 사용된다. 따라서 전체 문장은 분사구문 (Having read) + 주절(a reader can review) + 관계대명사절(that are presented) + 수동태(are supported by enough evidence)의 구조로 완성된다.

Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.

solution: verifying or validating it is not'이라는 문장을 영작하는 문제로, 부사절 접속사 'but'은 박스에서 제외되어 있으므로 등위접속사 'but'을 스스로 추가해야 한다. 박스에 제공된 단어들은 원형/기본형이므로 어형을 변형해야 한다. body:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight. For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
solution: ③ 글은 온라인 정보를 탐색할 때 여러 출처를 통해 정보를 검증하는 '측면 읽기(lateral reading)' 전략을 소개하고, 구체적인 학생 사례를 통해 그 활용 방법을 설명하므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ① 수직적 읽기는 글의 도입부에서 새 전략의 필요성을 언급하기 위해 잠깐 등장할 뿐, 글 전체의 주제인 측면 읽기 전략을 담지 못한다. ② 온라인 기사의 통계를 믿을 수 없다는 내용은 글에서 직접 언급되지 않았으며, 통계는 측면 읽기로 검증해야 할 정보의 사례로만 제시된다. ④ 과학 저널 접근법은 측면 읽기의 여러 방법 중 하나로 마지막 문장에 언급될 뿐, 글 전체가 전달하고자 하는 핵심 주제를 포괄하지 못한다. ⑤ 여러 출처가 혼란을 야기한다는 내용은 글에 없으며, 글의 논지와 정반대로 여러 출처 활용을 긍정적으로 권장하고 있다.
choices: Vertical Reading: The Traditional Foundation of Information Processing
Why Statistics in Online Articles Cannot Always Be Trusted
Lateral Reading: Navigating Online Information Through Multiple Sources
How to Access Scientific Journals for Health Research
More Sources, More Confusion: The Limits of Lateral Reading 1회차 실전 모의고사

Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to . They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently. As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact- checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.
solution: 빈칸 다음 문장에서 여러 사이트를 동시에 검토하는 브라우저 도구를 활용하고, 데이터를 교차 확인하며 주장을 평가한다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '저자의 주장의 신뢰성을 확인하다'는 의미의 ①이 가장 적절하다. ②가 온라인 출처 접근을 제한한다는 것은 디지털 측면 읽기의 목적과 반대된다. ③이 수직적 읽기 전략을 홍보한다는 것은 지문에서 수직적 읽기를 덜 최적화된 전략으로 언급하므로 부적절하다. ④가 사실 확인 없이 기사를 출판한다는 것은 지문의 내용과 정반대이다. ⑤가 이용 가능한 데이터의 양을 줄인다는 것은 인터넷의 방대한 정보를 활용한다는 지문 내용과 상반된다. 비상(홍) 4과

limit access to online sources
promote vertical reading strategies
publish articles without fact-checking

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절 한 것은?
Single-Source Reading In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as (A) "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.
solution: ③ (정답): 지문에서 (A) "vertical reading"은 단일 출처/ 텍스트 자체에 의존하여(relying on the text, based on only their text) 글쓴이의 신뢰성, 논리, 근거 등을 평가하는 읽기 방식이라고 명시되어 있다. 따라서 '하나의 텍스트 안에서 글쓴이의 신뢰성과 논리를 평가한다'가 가장 적절한 의미이다. ① (오답): 여러 출처를 비교하는 것은 수직적 읽기(vertical reading)가 아니라, 본문 마지막 문장 이후에 제시될 새로운 읽기 전략(수평적 읽기, lateral reading)에 해당한다. ② (오답): 독자의 경험을 우선시한다는 내용은 지문에 전혀 언급되어 있지 않다. ④ (오답): 기술 발전에 따라 읽기 전략을 바꾸는 것은 수직적 읽기의 한계를 지적하며 제시된 배경 문맥일 뿐, 수직적 읽기 자체의 개념 정의가 아니다. ⑤ (오답): 말하는 사람의 권위/신뢰성에 의존하는 것은 인쇄술 발달 이전 구전 시대(spoken word)의 정보 판단 방식에 해당한다.
choices: 여러 출처를 비교하여 정보의 신뢰성을 검증한다.
글쓴이의 주장보다 독자의 경험을 우선시한다.
하나의 텍스트 안에서 글쓴이의 신뢰성과 논리를 평가한다.
기술의 발전에 따라 읽기 전략을 유연하게 바꾼다.
말하는 사람의 권위에 의존하여 정보의 가치를 판단한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today's words, one could say that the pictures went "viral," and Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility." For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.
solution: credibility는 ‘신뢰성, 믿을 만함’을 의미한다. 유명 작가인 Doyle이 사진이 초자연적 현상의 증거라고 주장하면서 사람들은 그 사진을 진짜일 가능성이 높다고 믿게 되었다는 의미이다. 따라서 정답은 ① Doyle's support made people more likely to believe that the pictures were authentic.
choices: Doyle's support made people more likely to believe that the pictures were authentic.
Doyle's article helped the girls learn how to take more realistic pictures of fairies.
Doyle's fame allowed the pictures to become popular mainly among professional photographers.
Doyle's endorsement encouraged people to question whether the supernatural phenomena were real.
Doyle's article proved that the pictures had been scientifically verified as genuine.

body:
다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.
solution: ①이 정답이다. 글에서 필자는 "readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it"라며 독자가 정보를 평가하는 습관으로 lateral reading을 적극 권장하고 있으므로, 글의 목적으로 가장 적절하다. ② vertical reading이 읽기 속도를 향상시킨다는 내용은 언급되지 않았다. ③ 중립을 주장하는 저자를 비판하는 것이 아니라, 그럼에도 독자가 직접 신뢰성을 평가해야 한다고 말하는 것이 글의 핵심이다. ④ 데이터 신뢰성 확인을 위한 새로운 기술을 소개하는 내용은 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 미디어를 과도하게 소비하는 것의 위험성을 경고하는 내용은 언급되지 않았다. 비상(홍) 4과
choices: to recommend lateral reading as a habit for evaluating information
to explain how vertical reading improves reading speed
to criticize authors who claim to be neutral
to introduce new technology for checking data credibility
to warn readers about the dangers of consuming too much media

body:
다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.
solution: ①이 정답이다. 지문 마지막 문장에서 "media literacy is more important than ever"라고 직접 주장하고 있으므로, 글의 주장으로 가장 적절하다. ② 인터넷이 출판의 장벽을 없앴다는 것은 현황 설명일 뿐, 출판 기준을 따라야 한다는 주장은 언급되지 않았다. ③ 글은 첨단 기술이 속임수를 더 쉽게 만들 수 있다고 지적하나, 기술에 의존하지 말아야 한다는 주장은 하지 않았다. ④ 허위 주장을 퍼뜨리는 사람들을 처벌해야 한다는 내용은 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 요정의 사진 이야기는 글의 요지를 이끌어내기 위한 도입 사례일 뿐, 글의 주장은 아니다.
choices: 오늘날 정보 환경에서 미디어 리터러시를 갖춰야 한다.
인터넷에 글을 올리려면 출판 기준을 반드시 따라야 한다.
정보를 검증하려면 첨단 기술에 의존하지 말아야 한다.
허위 주장을 퍼뜨리는 사람들을 강력히 처벌해야 한다.
요정의 존재를 믿으려면 신뢰할 수 있는 사진이 있어야 한다. 유형보충독해

Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers ⓐspending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with ⓑmanaging their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are ⓒimplementing legal restrictions on minors' access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media
ⓓhave been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or maintain social media accounts and the other
ⓔgranted parents full access to their children's online activities.

다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 없는 것은?
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving. As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers' social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever- changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?
solution: ③이 정답이다. 지문에서 소셜 미디어는 새로운 우정을 발견하고 비슷한 관심사를 가진 사람들과 연결하는 플랫폼이라고 했다. 즉 기존 친구에게만 국한되지 않으므로, '기존 친구들과만 연결된다'는 진술은 추론할 수 없다. ① 지역 사회 내에서 정서적 지지가 부족한 청소년에게 소셜 미디어가 필수적인 정서적 지원을 제공한다고 했으므로 추론할 수 있다. ② 청소년이 생각, 경험, 재능을 공유함으로써 디지털 세계에서 자아 정체성을 찾을 수 있다고 했으므로 추론할 수 있다. ④ 청소년의 소셜 미디어 규제 문제가 여전히 열린 상태로 남아 있고 계속 변화한다고 했으므로 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 이 논쟁이 개인의 자유와 사회적 이익 사이의 근본적인 긴장을 보여준다고 했으므로 추론할 수 있다.
choices: Teenagers who lack local community support may benefit emotionally from social media.
Social media can help teenagers build a sense of who they are.
Social media helps teenagers stay connected with only their existing friends.
The debate over regulating teenagers' social media use has no clear resolution yet.

body:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고 르시오.
주어진 글:
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer.
(A) Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving. 1회차
(B) As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers' social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever- changing digital landscape.
(C) Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world.
solution: 주어진 글은 우려에도 불구하고 소셜 미디어의 중요한 이점을 인정하는 균형 잡힌 시각을 유지해야 한다는 필요성을 제시한다. (C)는 주어진 글에서 언급된 소셜 미디어의 이점을 구체화하며, 청소년이 자기표현, 새로운 우정, 비슷한 개인들과의 연결이라는 플랫폼으로서의 역할과 자아 정체성 형성을 설명한다. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers, and it offers essential emotional support.
→Not only

solution: A뿐만 아니라 B도'라는 의미를 나타내는 Not only A, but also B 구문에서 부정어구인 Not only가 강조를 위해 문장의 맨 앞으로 나가면 주어와 동사의 도치가 일어난다. 주어가 3인칭 단수(social media)이고 일반동사 현재시제 (provides)이므로, 의문문 어순과 동일하게 does + 주어 (social media) + 동사원형(provide) 어순으로 도치시킨 뒤 뒷절을 but (it) also offers~로 연결하는 것이 올바르다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of ⓐthem near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls
ⓑplaying with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article ⓒclaiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today's words, one could say ⓓthat the pictures went "viral," and Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility." For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. (가)오직 약 70년이 지나서야 그 소 녀들은 마침내 그 모든 것이 거짓으로 만들어졌음을 인정했다.
While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale
ⓔdemonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
solution: ④ 본문에서 소녀들은 거의 70년이 지나서야 거짓임을 인정했다고 했으므로, 사진이 찍힌 직후 솔직하게 고백했다는 설명은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ① 본문 첫 문장에서 개울가에서 요정과 노는 사진을 찍었다고 했으므로 옳다. ② 코난 도일이 초자연적 현상의 증거라는 글을 썼다고 했으므로 옳다. ③ 코난 도일의 지지가 신뢰성을 주었다고 했으므로 옳다. ⑤ 미디어 리터러시의 중요성을 보여주는 경고적 이야기라고 했으므로 옳다.
choices: 코팅리의 두 소녀는 정원 구석 개울가에서 요정과 노는 사진 을 찍었다.
아서 코난 도일 경은 소녀들의 사진이 초자연적 현상의 증거 라고 주장하는 글을 썼다.
코난 도일의 지지는 사진의 신뢰성을 높여주는 역할을 하였 다.
소녀들은 사진이 찍힌 직후 그것이 거짓으로 만들어진 것임 을 솔직하게 고백했다.
이 이야기는 디지털 시대에 미디어 리터러시의 중요성을 보 여주는 경고적 이야기이다.

While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale
ⓔdemonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.

밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ① them → themselves 문장의 주어는 two young girls(두 어린 소녀들)이며 자신들의 사진을 찍은 것이므로, 주어와 목적어가 동일한 대상을 가리키고 있다. 따라서 대명사 them이 아니라 재귀대명사 themselves로 고쳐야 올바르다. ② 5형식 지각동사 showed의 목적격보어로, 목적어인 the girls가 요정과 '놀고 있는' 능동 및 진행의 의미를 나타내므로 현재분사 playing은 올바르다. ③ 앞의 주절에 이어져 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사구문으로 올바르다. ④ 타동사 say 뒤에서 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사 that이며 뒤에 the pictures(주어) + went(동사) + viral(보어)로 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 적절하다. ⑤ 앞의 명사구 a cautionary tale을 뒤에서 수식하는 현재분사로 올바르다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 적절하도록 주어진 단어를 활용하여 쓰시오.
Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication (A) _____ to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a (B) _____ process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.
(A) _____ (claim)
(B) _____ (continue 또는 repeat)
solution: (A) claims: 양보의 복합관계부사절(No matter how + 형용사 + 주어 + 동사) 구조이다. 주어로 명사구 an author or publication이 왔으며, 접속사 or로 연결된 경우 단수 취급하므로 주어진 동사 claim을 3인칭 단수 현재형인 claims로 형태를 바꾸어 써야 한다. (B) continuous, repetitive: 뒤에 위치한 명사 process를 수식해 주는 형용사 자리가 되어야 한다. 따라서 동사 continue와 repeat를 각각 형용사 형태인 continuous와 repetitive로 변형하여 완성한다. 비상(홍) 4과 실전 모의고사 2회차

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's ⓐunderstandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from ⓑbeing fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to ⓒverify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or ⓓvalidating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and ⓔvalidity information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.
solution: ⑤ validity → valid 'validity'는 명사형으로, 뒤에 오는 명사 'information'을 수식하는 형용사 자리에는 형용사 'valid'가 와야 한다. 앞의 'reliable'과 마찬가지로 형용사가 명사를 수식하는 구조이므로, validity를 valid로 고쳐야 한다. ① 'it's understandable that ~' 구조에서 가주어 it에 대한 진주어절을 이끄는 형용사 보어로 understandable이 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 'prevent A from -ing' 구조로, 전치사 from 뒤에 동명사 being fooled가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 'know how to + 동사원형' 구조에서 동사원형 verify가 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 등위접속사 or로 verifying과 병렬 연결되는 동명사 validating이 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 낱 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes (A) [evaluate / evaluating] all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to (B) [determine / determined] the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving:
information does not remain still, so neither (C)
[should / should not] the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.
solution: (A) evaluating: 동사 makes의 목적어 자리이며, 뒤에 목적격 보어 a habit을 취하는 5형식 구문(make A B: A를 B로 만들다)이다. 따라서 동사원형 evaluate가 아닌 동명사 evaluating이 목적어로 와서 "모든 형태의 정보를 평가하는 것을 습관으로 만들다"라는 의미를 구성해야 한다. (B) determine: 앞에서 유도된 목적의 to부정사 구문(to survey ~ to determine ...)으로, to 뒤에는 동사원형이 위치해야 하므로 determine이 올바르다. (C) should: '~도 역시 그렇지 않다'라는 의미를 나타내는 neither + 조동사/be동사 + 주어 부정 도치 구문이다. 부어구 neither 자체에 이미 부정의 의미가 포함되어 있으므로, 조동사는 긍정형인 should를 써야 올바른 문법이 된다. (should not을 쓰면 이중 부정이 되어 어법상 틀림)
choices: evaluate - determine - should
evaluate - determined - should not
evaluating -  determine  - should
evaluating - determined - should
evaluating - determine - should not

In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies.
(A) For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.
(B) When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena.
(C) In today's words, one could say that the pictures went "viral," and Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility."
solution: 주어진 글은 1917년 영국 Cottingley에서 두 소녀가 요정과 함께 찍은 사진을 소개하며 이야기의 배경을 제시한다. (B)는 주어진 글의 사진을 Sherlock Holmes의 작가 Doyle이 접하고, 이것이 초자연적 현상의 증거라는 기사를 썼다는 내용으로, 주어진 글의 'pictures'를 직접 받아 전개된다. (C)는 'Doyle의 지지'라는 표현으로 (B)의 Doyle 기사 내용을 이어받아, 사진이 '바이럴'되고 신뢰성을 얻게 된 결과를 설명한다. (A)는 'the pictures were genuine'이라는 표현으로 (C)의 신뢰성 획득 상황을 이어받아, 소녀들이 오랫동안 사진이 진짜라고 주장하다 결국 조작임을 인정했다는 결말과 교훈으로 마무리된다. 따라서 (B)-(C)-(A)의 순서가 가장 적절하다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and ⓐwritten materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on ⓑthe passage to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only ⓓtheir text. Having read ⓒa book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making ⓔit necessary to change reading strategies.

윗글의 중심 내용을 가장 잘 나타내는 제목은?
solution: ② 지문은 수직적 읽기의 정의와 특징, 즉 단일 출처와 텍스트 자체의 논리에 의존하여 정보와 저자의 신뢰성을 평가하는 방식을 설명하고 있으므로 제목으로 적절하다. ① 인쇄술은 수직적 읽기가 등장하게 된 배경으로 짧게 언급되었을 뿐, 현대 사회 인쇄술의 역사 전체를 다룬 글이 아니다. ③ 디지털 기술의 발전으로 읽기 전략의 변화가 필요해졌다고 했을 뿐, 기술이 비판적 사고를 망쳤다는 내용은 없다. ④ 소셜 미디어상의 가짜 뉴스를 가려내는 구체적인 식별법에 대해서는 지문에서 다루지 않는다. ⑤ 구두 언어는 과거 지식 전달 방식의 예시로 서두에 잠시 등장할 뿐, 지문의 핵심 소재가 아니다.

body:
다음 글의 단락 중 "lateral reading의 개념·필요성"에 대 한 내용이 있는 단락을 찾아 기호를 쓰시오.
(A) Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight.
(B) For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
(C) Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
(D) As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.
→
solution: (A)에서는 lateral reading이 무엇인지와 왜 필요한지를 직접 설명하고 있다. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading" → lateral reading의 개념 제시 which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can → lateral reading의 방법 설명 This is useful because only one source is not enough → lateral reading의 필요성 제시 Checking information from multiple sources ... is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight → 여러 출처를 확인하는 이유와 효과 설명 반면, (B): lateral reading의 구체적인 활용 사례 (C): digital lateral reading의 장점과 활용 (D): fact-checkers의 lateral reading 활용 사례와 효과 따라서 “lateral reading의 개념·필요성”에 대한 내용이 있는 단락은 (A)이다.

In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. ⓐcredibility: the quality of being trusted and believed in
ⓑprevalent: not common or widespread in a particular area or at a particular time
ⓒvalidity: the quality of being based on truth or sound reasoning
ⓓexamine: to look at or consider something carefully in order to understand it
ⓔdetermine: to discover the facts about something
solution: ②가 정답이다. ② 제시된 풀이 'not common or widespread in a particular area or at a particular time(특정 지역이나 시기에 흔하지 않거나 널리 퍼지지 않은)'은 prevalent의 뜻과 반대이다. prevalent의 올바른 풀이는 'very common or widespread in a particular area or at a particular time(특정 지역이나 시기에 매우 흔하거나 널리 퍼진)'이다. ① credibility(신뢰성): 신뢰받고 믿어지는 질, 즉 신뢰할 수 있는 특성 ③ validity(타당성): 진실이나 건전한 추론에 기반한 특성 ④ examine(검토하다): 어떤 것을 이해하기 위해 주의 깊게 살펴보거나 고려하다 ⑤ determine(알아내다): 어떤 것에 대한 사실을 발견하다 비상(홍) 4과 실전 모의고사 2회차

In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not ⓐthat was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ 'This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading"'에서 분석의 유형이 "수직 읽기"로 불리는 것이므로, 수동태 be described as가 올바르게 쓰였다. ① that → what 'The credibility of the speaker, not ⓐthat was said'에서 전치사 없이 동사 was의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절이 필요하다. 접속사 that은 명사절에서 주어 역할을 할 수 없으므로, 주어 기능을 하는 관계대명사 what으로 고쳐야 한다. ② have → had 'When the printing press introduced books ~ and written materials became more prevalent'라는 과거 시제의 종속절과 호응하는 주절이므로, 과거 시제 had를 써야 한다. 현재형 have는 시제 일치에 어긋난다. ④ basing → based 'their references basing on only their text'에서 references(참고 문헌)는 텍스트에 기반되는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 based를 써야 한다. 능동의 현재분사 basing은 어법상 틀리다. ⑤ necessarily → necessary 'making it necessarily to change reading strategies'에서 make + 목적어(it) + 목적격 보어 구문이 쓰였다. 목적격 보어 자리에는 형용사가 와야 하므로 부사 necessarily를 형용사 necessary로 고쳐야 한다.

다음 단락들 중 "개인 독자에서 나아가 기업 및 전문적인 영 역에서의 활용 사례"를 이야기하는 단락은 어느 것인지 찾 아 기호를 쓰시오.
(A) Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight.
(B) For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
(C) Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
(D) As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.
→
solution: (D)는 lateral reading이 개인 독자의 활용을 넘어 기업 및 전문적인 영역에서 활용되는 사례를 설명하고 있다. 특히, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims에서 기업(some companies)이 전문적인 사실 확인 담당자(fact-checkers)를 고용하여 글의 내용을 검증하는 사례를 제시한다. 이어 뉴스 기관이 기업 합병에 관한 기사를 게시하기 전에 여러 출처의 정보를 교차 확인하는 구체적인 사례를 들어, 전문적인 영역에서 lateral reading이 활용되는 방식을 설명한다. 반면, (A): lateral reading의 개념과 필요성 (B): 개인 독자(학생)의 구체적인 활용 사례 (C): 개인과 기업을 포함한 독자들이 lateral reading을 활용하는 일반적인 장점과 효과 (D): 기업 및 전문적인 영역에서의 구체적인 활용 사례와 효과 따라서 정답은 (D)이다.

글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절 한 곳을 고르시오.
Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. ( ⓐ ) Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? ( ⓑ ) In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. ( ⓒ ) Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. ( ⓓ ) This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. ( ⓔ ) In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.
solution: 주어진 문장은 'however'라는 역접 담화 표지와 함께 인터넷이 독자들로 하여금 신뢰할 수 있고 타당한 정보를 찾기 어렵게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있으므로, 이 앞에는 인터넷이 출판의 장벽을 제거했다는 긍정적 측면이 언급되어야 하고, 이 뒤에는 그러한 정보 환경에 대한 대응 또는 평가가 이어져야 한다. ⑤ 앞 문장은 In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet.(과거의 출판 기준) 이고, ⑤ 뒤 문장은 '이러한 환경에서 미디어 리터러시가 그 어느 때보다 중요하다'는 평가이다. 주어진 문장이 ⑤ 자리에 들어가면 출판 장벽 제거(긍정) → 정보 신뢰성 저하(부정, however) → 미디어 리터러시의 중요성(결론)으로 논리가 자연스럽게 이어진다. 따라서 ⑤ 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.

'Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit'은 조동사 did가 주어 the girls 앞으로 올바르게 도치된 구문이다. 따라서 ④가 정답이다. ① played → playing 목적격보어 자리에서 the girls가 fairies와 직접 노는 행위의 주체이므로 능동의 현재분사 playing이 와야 한다. 과거분사 played는 수동('~에 의해 놀아지다')의 의미가 되어 문맥에 맞지 않는다. ② claiming what → claiming that claim의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 자리이다. 명사절 이하 'the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena'는 주어·동사·보어를 갖춘 완전한 절이므로, 불완전한 절을 이끄는 what이 아니라 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사 that을 써야 한다. ③ had given → gave 앞 절의 동사 went와 등위접속사 and로 연결된 병렬 구조로, 같은 시간대의 과거 사건을 나열하고 있다. 단순과거 gave가 적절하며, had given(과거완료)은 다른 과거 사건보다 먼저 일어난 사건에 쓰이므로 이 문맥에서는 어법상 틀리다. ⑤ demonstrated → demonstrating 선행사 a cautionary tale을 뒤에서 수식하는 분사 자리이다. 'a cautionary tale이 중요성을 보여주다'라는 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 demonstrating이 와야 한다. 과거 동사형 demonstrated를 쓰면 접속사 없이 한 문장에 본동사가 두 개(may be, demonstrated)가 되는 오류가 발생한다. 비상(홍) 4과

주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고 르시오.
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness.
(A) Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text.
(B) However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.
(C) When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading."
solution: 주어진 글은 과거에 지식이 구전으로 전달되었고, 신뢰성의 기준이 화자의 권위에 있었음을 소개한다. (C)는 주어진 글의 구전 시대와 대비하여 인쇄기의 등장으로 서면 자료가 보급되면서 독자들이 새로운 비판적 평가 능력을 갖추어야 했고, 이러한 분석 방식이 '수직적 읽기'로 불린다고 소개하며 자연스럽게 이어진다. (A)는 (C)의 마지막에 등장한 'vertical reading'을 첫 문장의 주어로 받아, 수직적 읽기의 구체적인 방법—저자의 신뢰성, 논리, 참고문헌을 텍스트 안에서만 검토하는 것—을 상세히 설명한다. (B)는 (A)에서 설명한 텍스트 내부 분석 방식의 한계를 'However'로 전환하며, 기술의 발전이 글쓰기와 출판 환경을 바꾸어 읽기 전략의 변화가 필요해졌다는 결론으로 마무리한다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B)의 순서가 가장 적절하다.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 모두 고르면?
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight. For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
① Vertical reading has become obsolete now that lateral reading has been introduced.
② Lateral reading is based on checking information across a variety of source types.
③ The student in the example mainly used news sites to double-check the statistics she read.
④ Opening multiple browser tabs is described as a strategy exclusive to scientific research.
⑤ Lateral reading can involve going straight to a scientific journal to check a primary source.
solution: ② 지문에서는 텍스트, 이미지, 영상 등 다양한 유형의 콘텐츠를 가진 여러 자료로부터 정보를 확인하는 것이 도움이 된다고 명시하고 있으므로, 가로 읽기가 다양한 유형의 자료를 확인하는 것에 기반한다는 내용과 일치한다. ⑤ 지문에서는 학생이 학술지 원문으로 직접 가서 원출처로부터 읽을 수 있다고 명시하고 있으므로, 가로 읽기가 학술지로 직접 가서 원출처를 확인하는 것을 포함할 수 있다는 내용과 일치한다. ① 지문 첫 문장에서 '세로 읽기는 여전히 유용하다'고 명시하고 있으므로, 세로 읽기가 더 이상 쓸모없어졌다는 것은 지문의 내용과 정반대이다. ③ 지문에서는 학생이 어느 쪽을 '주로' 이용했는지에 대한 비중은 언급하지 않는다. ④ 여러 브라우저 탭을 여는 것은 학생의 사례에서 일반적인 가로 읽기 전략의 실천 방법으로 제시될 뿐, 과학 연구에만 국한된 전략이라는 내용은 지문과 다르다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text.
(A)After a reader has read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies. Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.
